unmapped_findings: Pure iron corresponds to the polycrystalline alloy with nominal 0 at.% Al in Table 1; its real Al content was not determined (n.d.) and its carbon content is 100 wt.ppm, with Si and other impurities not listed.

The yield stress of pure iron was obtained by averaging the data for 3 rather coarse-grained specimens (with perpendicular orientations in the original ingot) of iron prepared by electron-beam remelting (b0032).

Pure iron provides the 0 at.% Al anchor point of the linear yield-stress vs Al-content relationship; the interpolating straight lines indicate a yield-stress increase of 21 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-2 s^-1 and 23 MPa per at.% Al at 10^-4 s^-1 (b0032).

The overall solid-solution hardening coefficient of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys with 0-18 at.% Al is about 2.2 GPa, which is not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature; the linear increase is described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys (b0058).
In Fig. 3 at 0 at.% Al the open circle (10^-2 s^-1) lies on the 100 MPa gridline and the filled circle (10^-4 s^-1) sits between the 0 and 100 MPa lines (figure_003).

Pure iron was tested in compression (both strain rates) at room temperature as part of the composition-dependent yield-stress study; no tensile ductility, hardness or fracture data are reported specifically for the pure iron specimen.
